subject.title: acp: assistant text corrupted when Gateway revises in-progress output (non-append revision mis-sliced)

question: How should the ACP bridge represent Gateway replace=true revisions when ACP message chunks cannot reliably retract already-emitted text?
rationale: The root cause is clear, but the durable fix depends on a cross-protocol behavior choice rather than a purely mechanical slice replacement.

options.title: Choose a conservative ACP mapping
options.body: Buffer or otherwise avoid unretractable provisional output when Gateway replacement semantics are possible, then add text and thinking regression tests.

options.title: Use a new-message fallback
options.body: Emit replacement snapshots under a new ACP message identity, accepting that some clients may show both stale and corrected messages instead of one corrected answer.

options.title: Define a client extension
options.body: Depend on ACP metadata or a known client capability only if maintainers are willing to document behavior for clients that ignore it.

recommendation.title: Choose a conservative ACP mapping
recommendation.body: Buffer or otherwise avoid unretractable provisional output when Gateway replacement semantics are possible, then add text and thinking regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the ACP bridge and Gateway protocol boundary where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
